chunks: And from him, from ʿAmmār ibn al-Mubārak, from Ẓarīf ibn Nāṣiḥ, from al-Qāsim ibn al-Walīd al-Ghassānī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him, ‘May I be made your ransom, the daytime salat of the nawafil—how many is it?’ He said, ‘Sixteen. Whichever hours of the day you wish to perform them, you may perform them, except that if you perform them at their proper times, that is more excellent.’

key_terms.النَّهَارِ: the daytime period in which these nawafil are performed
key_terms.النَّوَافِلِ: supererogatory prayers performed in addition to the obligatory salat
key_terms.سَاعَاتِ: hours or portions of the day
key_terms.سِتَّ عَشْرَةَ: sixteen, the stated number of daytime nawafil units
key_terms.صَلَاةُ: salat (prayer), referring here to the recommended ritual prayer

ai.seo_question: How many daytime nawafil are there, and can they be prayed at any time during the day?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the nawafil of the day consist of sixteen rakʿahs. It also indicates flexibility in performing them during the daytime, while affirming that observing their designated times is more excellent.
